metadata.title: Playing Atari with Deep Reinforcement Learning
metadata.authors: Mnih, Kavukcuoglu, Silver, Graves, Antonoglou, Wierstra, Riedmiller

nodes.name: Atari Game Control from Raw Pixels
nodes.statement: Learn control policies for Atari 2600 games directly from high-dimensional raw pixel input ($210 \times 160$ RGB at 60Hz) using only the video, reward, and terminal signals.
nodes.statement_clean: Learn to play Atari games end-to-end from screen pixels using reinforcement learning.

nodes.name: Agent-Environment Interaction
nodes.statement: An agent interacts with environment $\mathcal{E}$ in a sequence of actions $a_t \in \mathcal{A}=\{1,\ldots,K\}$, observations $x_t \in \mathbb{R}^d$ (raw pixels), and rewards $r_t$ (change in game score).

nodes.name: State Sequence
nodes.statement: Since observations are partially observed (perceptual aliasing), define $s_t = x_1, a_1, x_2, \ldots, a_{t-1}, x_t$; sequences are assumed to terminate, giving a finite MDP with each sequence as a distinct state.

nodes.name: Discounted Return
nodes.statement: Future discounted return at time $t$: $R_t = \sum_{t'=t}^{T} \gamma^{t'-t} r_{t'}$, where $T$ is the terminal time-step and $\gamma \in (0,1]$ is the discount factor.

nodes.name: Optimal Action-Value Function
nodes.statement: $Q^*(s,a) = \max_{\pi} \mathbb{E}\left[ R_t \mid s_t = s, a_t = a, \pi \right]$, the maximum expected return achievable from state $s$ taking action $a$ under any policy $\pi$.

nodes.name: Q-Network
nodes.statement: A neural network function approximator with weights $\theta$ used to estimate the action-value function: $Q(s,a;\theta) \approx Q^*(s,a)$.

nodes.name: Behaviour Distribution
nodes.statement: $\rho(s,a)$ is a probability distribution over sequences $s$ and actions $a$ from which training samples are drawn during off-policy learning.

nodes.name: Experience Replay Memory
nodes.statement: Store agent experiences $e_t = (s_t, a_t, r_t, s_{t+1})$ in a dataset $\mathcal{D} = e_1, \ldots, e_N$ pooled over many episodes; Q-learning updates use minibatches $e \sim \mathcal{D}$ drawn at random.

nodes.name: Preprocessing Function $\phi$
nodes.statement: $\phi$ converts raw $210\times 160$ RGB frames to gray-scale, downsamples to $110\times 84$, crops to $84\times 84$, and stacks the last $4$ frames to produce the Q-network input.

nodes.name: Deep Q-Network (DQN) Architecture
nodes.statement: CNN with input $84\times 84\times 4$; conv1: $16$ filters $8\times 8$ stride $4$ + ReLU; conv2: $32$ filters $4\times 4$ stride $2$ + ReLU; FC: $256$ ReLU units; output: one linear unit per action.
nodes.statement_clean: Convolutional Q-network with two conv layers, one fully-connected hidden layer, and one output per action.

nodes.name: Bellman Equation for $Q^*$
nodes.statement: $Q^*(s,a) = \mathbb{E}_{s' \sim \mathcal{E}}\left[ r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q^*(s',a') \mid s, a \right]$.
nodes.origin_citation: Sutton & Barto, Reinforcement Learning: An Introduction

nodes.name: Q-Learning Loss
nodes.statement: $L_i(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{s,a \sim \rho(\cdot)}\left[ (y_i - Q(s,a;\theta_i))^2 \right]$ where $y_i = \mathbb{E}_{s' \sim \mathcal{E}}\left[ r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a';\theta_{i-1}) \mid s,a \right]$.

nodes.name: Q-Learning Gradient
nodes.statement: $\nabla_{\theta_i} L_i(\theta_i) = \mathbb{E}_{s,a \sim \rho(\cdot); s' \sim \mathcal{E}}\left[ (r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(s',a';\theta_{i-1}) - Q(s,a;\theta_i)) \nabla_{\theta_i} Q(s,a;\theta_i) \right]$.

nodes.name: Convergence of Value Iteration
nodes.statement: The value iteration update $Q_{i+1}(s,a) = \mathbb{E}\left[ r + \gamma \max_{a'} Q_i(s',a') \mid s,a \right]$ converges to the optimal action-value function: $Q_i \to Q^*$ as $i \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Q-Learning
nodes.statement: Online model-free off-policy temporal-difference learning algorithm that estimates $Q^*$ via stochastic samples from emulator and behaviour distribution.

nodes.name: Deep Q-Learning with Experience Replay
nodes.statement: Deep Q-learning algorithm: maintain replay memory $\mathcal{D}$ of transitions, act $\epsilon$-greedy w.r.t. $Q(\phi(s),a;\theta)$, sample minibatches from $\mathcal{D}$ and perform SGD on the squared TD error.

nodes.name: Neural Fitted Q-learning (NFQ)
nodes.statement: Batch Q-learning method that optimises the squared TD loss using RPROP; cost per iteration scales with dataset size.

nodes.name: TD-Gammon
nodes.statement: On-policy TD($\lambda$) algorithm that approximates $V(s)$ with a multilayer perceptron, trained from self-play, achieving super-human backgammon.

nodes.name: Sarsa Baseline (linear)
nodes.statement: Sarsa with hand-engineered linear features over Atari frames; baseline reported in Bellemare et al.

nodes.name: Contingency Baseline
nodes.statement: Sarsa-style learner augmented with a learned representation of the screen regions under the agent's control.

nodes.name: HyperNEAT (HNeat) Evolutionary Policy Search
nodes.statement: Evolutionary algorithm that evolves a separate neural network strategy per Atari game; reported as HNeat Best (object detector features) and HNeat Pixel.

nodes.name: RMSProp
nodes.statement: Adaptive per-parameter learning-rate stochastic gradient method used to train DQN with minibatches of size $32$.

nodes.name: Seven-Game Atari Benchmark
nodes.statement: DQN evaluated on Beam Rider, Breakout, Enduro, Pong, Q*bert, Seaquest, Space Invaders with the same network, hyperparameters, and learning algorithm; rewards clipped to $\{-1,0,+1\}$ during training; trained $10$M frames with replay $1$M.

nodes.name: Training Stability Curves
nodes.statement: On Breakout and Seaquest the average reward per episode is noisy but the average max predicted $Q$ on a held-out set of states increases smoothly during training; no divergence observed.

nodes.name: Value Function Visualization on Seaquest
nodes.statement: Predicted value rises when an enemy appears (point A), peaks as a torpedo is about to hit (point B), and falls back after the enemy disappears (point C), illustrating that DQN tracks task-relevant events.

nodes.name: DQN vs Baselines and Human Scores
nodes.statement: DQN achieves $4092, 168, 470, 20, 1952, 1705, 581$ on (B. Rider, Breakout, Enduro, Pong, Q*bert, Seaquest, S. Invaders), beating Random / Sarsa / Contingency on all seven games and beating an expert human on Breakout, Enduro, and Pong.

nodes.name: Frame-Skipping
nodes.statement: Agent selects an action every $k$-th frame and repeats it on skipped frames; $k=4$ for all games except Space Invaders, where $k=3$ is used so that lasers remain visible.

nodes.name: Reward Clipping
nodes.statement: All positive rewards clipped to $+1$ and negative rewards to $-1$ during training to allow a single learning rate across games; this discards reward magnitude information.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-greedy Annealing
nodes.statement: Behaviour policy is $\epsilon$-greedy with $\epsilon$ annealed linearly from $1$ to $0.1$ over the first million frames and held at $0.1$ thereafter.

nodes.name: Advantages of Experience Replay
nodes.statement: Experience replay (i) reuses each step in many updates (data efficiency), (ii) breaks correlations between consecutive samples reducing update variance, and (iii) averages the behaviour distribution to avoid oscillations and divergence.

nodes.name: Divergence with Nonlinear Off-policy Q-learning
nodes.statement: Combining model-free Q-learning with nonlinear function approximators or off-policy learning can cause the Q-network to diverge.

nodes.name: Initialize replay memory and Q-network
nodes.statement: Initialize replay memory $\mathcal{D}$ to capacity $N$; initialize action-value function $Q$ with random weights $\theta$.

nodes.name: Episode loop
nodes.statement: For episode $=1,M$: initialise sequence $s_1 = \{x_1\}$ and preprocessed sequence $\phi_1 = \phi(s_1)$.

nodes.name: $\epsilon$-greedy action selection
nodes.statement: With probability $\epsilon$ select a random action $a_t$; otherwise select $a_t = \arg\max_{a} Q(\phi(s_t), a; \theta)$.

nodes.name: Execute action and observe transition
nodes.statement: Execute $a_t$ in the emulator and observe reward $r_t$ and next image $x_{t+1}$; set $s_{t+1} = s_t, a_t, x_{t+1}$ and preprocess $\phi_{t+1} = \phi(s_{t+1})$.

nodes.name: Store transition in replay memory
nodes.statement: Store transition $(\phi_t, a_t, r_t, \phi_{t+1})$ in $\mathcal{D}$.

nodes.name: Sample minibatch and compute targets
nodes.statement: Sample random minibatch of transitions $(\phi_j, a_j, r_j, \phi_{j+1})$ from $\mathcal{D}$; set $y_j = r_j$ if $\phi_{j+1}$ terminal, else $y_j = r_j + \gamma \max_{a'} Q(\phi_{j+1}, a'; \theta)$.

nodes.name: Gradient descent step
nodes.statement: Perform a gradient descent step on $(y_j - Q(\phi_j, a_j; \theta))^2$ following the gradient in equation EP238.3.
